q: The fortune teller's words were deliberately ___, allowing several interpretations.
explain: Ambiguous = can be understood in more than one way. Example: an ambiguous ending.

q: That argument doesn't ___ water.
explain: Hold water = be logical. Example: His excuse doesn't hold water.

q: We must not ___ how important sleep is for learning.
explain: Underestimate = think something is smaller than it is. Example: Don't underestimate her.

q: Her idea for a school on Mars was met with widespread ___.
explain: Scepticism (noun) = doubt. Example: The news was met with scepticism.

q: The two teams ___ a compromise after hours of arguing about the rules.
explain: Hammer out = reach an agreement after hard discussion. Example: They hammered out a deal.

q: The pirate's claims are not ___ by the evidence.
explain: Substantiate = prove with evidence. Example: Can you substantiate that?

notes.subsidised: Subsidise = pay part of the cost.

q: He tends to ___ around the bush instead of answering directly.
explain: Beat around the bush = avoid the main point. Example: Stop beating around the bush!

q: Discovering water on the Moon will have far-___ consequences.
explain: Far-reaching = affecting many things. Example: far-reaching changes.

q: Her ___ analysis exposed several flaws in the escape plan.
explain: Incisive = sharp and clear. Example: an incisive question.

q: The online game chat became increasingly ___, with insults on both sides.
explain: Acrimonious = angry and bitter. Example: an acrimonious argument.

q: With ___, it's clear the plan was flawed from the start.
explain: Hindsight = understanding after something happens. Example: In hindsight, I should have studied.

notes.oversight: Oversight = a mistake by not noticing.

q: The first Moon landing was a ___ moment in human history.
explain: Pivotal = central, causing change. Example: a pivotal match.

q: She ___ her rival's argument point by point in the debate club.
explain: Dismantle = take apart (also arguments). Example: She dismantled his excuse.

q: His apology seemed ___ rather than sincere.
explain: Perfunctory = done quickly without care. Example: a perfunctory wave.

q: Let's not jump to ___.
explain: Jump to conclusions = decide too fast. Example: Don't jump to conclusions!

q: The new buddy scheme aims to ___ the gap between older and younger pupils.
explain: Bridge the gap = make a difference smaller. Example: bridge the gap between cultures.

notes.build: Build the gap isn't a collocation.
notes.broaden: Broaden would make the gap bigger.

q: The referee's decision ___ a storm of criticism.
explain: Spark = cause suddenly. Example: The news sparked excitement.

q: The report paints a rather ___ picture of the coral reef's future.
explain: Bleak = without hope. Example: a bleak winter.

q: She has a ___ grasp of how black holes work.
explain: A firm grasp = good understanding. Example: a firm grasp of maths.

q: The two clubs remain ___ apart on where to go for the trip.
explain: Poles apart = completely different. Example: The twins are poles apart.

notes.miles: People say 'miles apart', but the idiom for completely opposite views is 'poles apart'.
notes.streets: Streets ahead means much better, not different.

q: His plan ___ on the assumption that the cat will stay asleep.
explain: Hinge on = depend completely on. Example: Everything hinges on the weather.

notes.leans: Lean on = depend on a person.

q: The school trip was ___ from the start by bad weather.
explain: Dogged by = troubled again and again by. Example: dogged by injuries.

q: Which word means 'to make a situation worse'?
explain: Exacerbate = make worse. Example: Scratching exacerbates the itch.

notes.exonerate: Exonerate = show someone is not guilty.

q: Her decision to leave the band came as a bolt from the ___.
explain: A bolt from the blue = a total surprise. Example: The news came as a bolt from the blue.

q: The plan for a school garden received ___ support from every class.
explain: Unanimous = everyone agrees. Example: a unanimous vote.

notes.universal agreement: Universal agreement is a noun phrase, not an adjective.

q: The student council will ___ the matter at its next meeting.
explain: Address a matter = deal with it. Example: We'll address your question.

q: Critics ___ the inventor's plan as unrealistic.
explain: Dismiss as = reject as not worth considering. Example: She dismissed it as a joke.

q: He gave a ___ account of events, leaving nothing out.
explain: Meticulous = very careful about details. Example: meticulous notes.

q: The football final was ___ by a series of nasty fouls.
explain: Marred by = spoiled by. Example: The day was marred by rain.

notes.marked down: Marked down = lower price or score.

q: The team's confidence is at an all-time ___ after five losses.
explain: An all-time low = the lowest ever. Example: Prices hit an all-time low.

q: The new student was so ___ that she hardly said a word all week.
explain: Reticent = not willing to say much. Example: He was reticent about his plans.

notes.reluctant to: Reluctant to needs a verb after it.

q: Tardigrades are incredibly ___: they can survive even in space.
explain: Resilient = able to survive or recover from difficult conditions. Example: a resilient plant.

notes.fragile: Fragile means easily broken, the opposite.
notes.reticent: Reticent = quiet and unwilling to talk.

q: The volcano has been ___ for centuries, but it could erupt again.
explain: Dormant = sleeping or inactive for now. Example: a dormant volcano.

notes.obsolete: Obsolete = no longer used, for objects or ideas.

q: Floppy disks are now completely ___.
explain: Obsolete = out of date, no longer used. Example: obsolete technology.

notes.extinct: Extinct is for animals and volcanoes.
notes.ancient: Ancient means very old, but not necessarily unused.

q: Her excuse for missing practice was ___: nobody believed it.
explain: Implausible = hard to believe. Example: an implausible story.

q: After the storm, a power cut was ___.
explain: Inevitable = certain to happen. Example: Change is inevitable.

q: Your advice on the science project was ___. Thank you!
explain: Invaluable = extremely useful (NOT 'not valuable'). Example: invaluable help.

notes.invalid: Invalid = not legally or officially acceptable.

q: He seemed completely ___ to the result; he just shrugged.
explain: Indifferent = not interested or caring. Example: She was indifferent to praise.

q: Pip was ___ when he was blamed for something his brother did.
explain: Indignant = angry because something is unfair. Example: She was indignant at the accusation.

q: The inventor came up with an ___ way to recycle plastic bottles.
explain: Ingenious = cleverly original. Example: an ingenious gadget.

q: Kangaroos are ___ to Australia.
explain: Indigenous = native to a place. Example: indigenous plants.

notes.foreign: Foreign = from another country, the opposite.

q: Toddlers are naturally ___; they ask 'why?' all day.
explain: Inquisitive = curious, eager to learn. Example: an inquisitive puppy.

q: Grey squirrels are an ___ species in Britain.
explain: Invasive = spreading into a new place and causing harm. Example: invasive weeds.

notes.endemic: Endemic = found naturally only in one place.

q: When I asked who ate the cake, my brother was very ___.
explain: Evasive = avoiding giving a clear answer. Example: an evasive reply.

notes.candid: Candid = honest and direct, the opposite.

q: She gave a ___ account of her mistake, hiding nothing.
explain: Candid = honest and direct. Example: a candid interview.

notes.cryptic: Cryptic = mysterious and hard to understand.

q: The pirate left a ___ message that took weeks to decode.
explain: Cryptic = mysterious, with a hidden meaning. Example: a cryptic crossword.

notes.lucid: Lucid = clear and easy to understand.

q: The teacher's explanation of black holes was wonderfully ___.
explain: Lucid = clear and easy to understand. Example: a lucid explanation.

notes.opaque: Opaque = hard to understand (or see through).
notes.obscure: Obscure = not well known or unclear.

q: The robot's movements were so ___ that it looked almost human.
explain: Fluid = smooth and graceful. Example: fluid dance moves.

notes.stagnant: Stagnant = not moving, often dirty water.

q: The pond water was ___ and smelled terrible.
explain: Stagnant (water) = not flowing, often dirty. Example: stagnant water breeds mosquitoes.

notes.stationary: Stationary = not moving, used for vehicles and objects.

q: Our team's ___ effort finally paid off in the final.
explain: Relentless = never stopping or easing. Example: relentless rain.

q: Please keep your answers ___ to the question.
explain: Relevant to = connected with. Example: That's not relevant to the debate.

q: Bats are ___ on their hearing to find food in the dark.
explain: Reliant on = depending on. Example: We're reliant on volunteers.

notes.reliable: Reliable = can be trusted; it doesn't take on.

q: The new rule aims to ___ bullying in the playground.
explain: Curb = limit or control something bad. Example: curb your spending.

notes.cultivate: Cultivate = grow or develop, the opposite.

q: Reading widely helps you ___ a love of language.
explain: Cultivate = develop carefully over time. Example: cultivate a habit.

q: Overfishing has ___ the number of cod in the North Sea.
explain: Deplete = reduce the amount of something. Example: depleted energy.

notes.replenished: Replenished = filled up again, the opposite.

q: Scientists hope to ___ malaria within twenty years.
explain: Eradicate = destroy completely. Example: eradicate a disease.

notes.evacuate: Evacuate = move people out of danger.

q: The ancient wall painting ___ a battle between two dragons.
explain: Depict = show in a picture or describe. Example: The film depicts life in space.

q: The team tried to ___ the new kid, inviting him to every game.
explain: Include = make someone part of a group. Example: include everyone.

q: Bad weather may ___ a launch this week.
explain: Preclude = prevent, make impossible. Example: His injury precludes him from playing.

q: A short speech will ___ the awards ceremony.
explain: Precede = come before. Example: Lightning precedes thunder.

q: After the floods, the water slowly began to ___.
explain: Recede = move back or further away. Example: The tide receded.

q: Finally, the champion had to ___ that her rival had played better.
explain: Concede = admit, often unwillingly. Example: He conceded defeat.

notes.conceive: Conceive = imagine or form an idea.

q: Chameleons can ___ themselves by changing colour.
explain: Camouflage = hide by blending in. Example: Tigers' stripes camouflage them.

q: The detective managed to ___ the culprit's plan.
explain: Thwart = stop someone's plan. Example: Police thwarted the robbery.

q: Cacti ___ in hot, dry deserts.
explain: Thrive = grow and develop well. Example: Children thrive on praise.

q: Without rain, the sunflowers began to ___.
explain: Wither = become dry and weak. Example: The leaves withered.

q: The number of wild tigers has ___ to just a few thousand.
explain: Dwindle = gradually become smaller. Example: Our supplies dwindled.

q: Ticket sales for the school play ___ after the great reviews.
explain: Soar = rise quickly to a high level. Example: Temperatures soared.

q: The temperature ___ to minus twenty overnight.
explain: Plummet = fall very fast. Example: The rock plummeted into the sea.

notes.escalated: Escalated = became more serious or intense.

q: The small argument ___ into a huge row about the game rules.
explain: Escalate = become more serious. Example: The conflict escalated.

q: Once the storm ___, we went out to look at the damage.
explain: Subside = become less strong. Example: The pain subsided.

q: The scientist's theory ___ a lot of attention online.
explain: Attract attention. Example: The bright colours attracted attention.

q: The two friends ___ a lasting friendship at summer camp.
explain: Forge a friendship/link = build a strong one. Example: They forged close ties.

notes.founded on: Founded on needs a noun after it.

q: We had to ___ a balance between homework and fun.
explain: Strike a balance = find a good middle point. Example: strike a balance between work and play.

notes.hit: Hit a balance isn't the collocation.

q: His speech ___ a chord with everyone who had moved schools.
explain: Strike a chord = make people feel sympathy or connection. Example: Her story struck a chord with me.

notes.played: Played a chord is music, not this idiom.
notes.hit on: Hit on = think of an idea.
notes.rang: Rang a bell = sounded familiar, a different idiom.

q: The robot competition ___ fierce rivalry between the schools.
explain: Spark rivalry/debate/interest = cause it to start. Example: The film sparked a debate.

q: The class ___ a heated debate about zoos.
explain: Engage in = take part in (formal). Example: engage in conversation.

notes.involved on: Involved on isn't English: involved in.

q: Our school places great ___ on kindness.
explain: Place emphasis on = treat as important. Example: We place emphasis on safety.

notes.stress on: The on is already in the sentence, so stress on repeats it.

q: The new evidence ___ doubt on the old theory.
explain: Cast doubt on = make something seem less certain. Example: The results cast doubt on his claim.

q: She ___ a lot of thought into her birthday present for me.
explain: Put thought/effort into. Example: He put a lot of effort into it.

q: The rescue dog ___ a vital role in finding the lost hikers.
explain: Play a role/part in. Example: Diet plays a role in health.

notes.did: Did a role isn't the collocation.
notes.acted: Acted a role is theatre language, not this meaning.

q: We need to ___ into account how tired the younger kids are.
explain: Take into account = consider. Example: Take the weather into account.

q: The professor's talk ___ light on how stars are born.
explain: Shed (or throw) light on = help explain. Example: The diary sheds light on her life.

notes.gave off: Gave off = produced, like heat or smell.
notes.made: Made light of = treated as unimportant.

q: Our teacher ___ the importance of checking our work.
explain: Stress the importance of = emphasise. Example: She stressed the need for safety.

notes.pressured: Pressured = pushed someone to do something.

q: The flood caused ___ damage to the village library.
explain: Extensive damage = a large amount. Example: extensive research.

notes.expansive: Expansive = covering a wide area, or friendly and open.

q: The game has a ___ following among teenagers.
explain: A loyal following = fans who stay with it. Example: The band has a loyal following.

notes.royal: Royal = connected with kings and queens.
notes.faithful to: Faithful to needs an object and doesn't fit before following.

q: There's a ___ chance the comet will be visible tonight.
explain: A slim chance = very small. Example: a slim chance of winning.

notes.thin: Thin chance isn't the usual collocation.
notes.narrow: Narrow goes with escape or victory.

q: We won by a ___ margin: just one point.
explain: A narrow margin/victory/escape. Example: a narrow escape.

notes.thin: Thin margin isn't the usual collocation.

q: The penguins huddled together to ___ the bitter cold.
explain: Withstand = resist something strong. Example: built to withstand earthquakes.

notes.uphold: Uphold = support a rule or decision.

q: The fire alarm ___ just as the exam began.
explain: Go off = start ringing (an alarm). Example: My alarm went off at six.

notes.broke out: Break out = start suddenly (a fire, war).

q: A fire ___ in the science lab, but nobody was hurt.
explain: Break out = start suddenly (fire, war, disease). Example: Chickenpox broke out at school.

notes.broke up: Break up = end a relationship, or a term ending.
notes.broke off: Break off = stop suddenly, or separate.

q: The team ___ the challenge with enthusiasm.
explain: Rise to the challenge/occasion = deal with it well. Example: She rose to the occasion.

q: It took the class a while to ___ the new seating plan.
explain: Warm to = start to like. Example: I warmed to the idea.

notes.warm up: Warm up = get ready, or get hotter.

q: The clues didn't ___. Someone must be lying.
explain: Add up = make sense. Example: His story doesn't add up.

q: I can't ___ what the sign says. It's too far away.
explain: Make out = see or hear with difficulty. Example: I could just make out a figure.

notes.make up: Make up = invent, or become friends again.

q: The thief ___ with the golden egg!
explain: Make off with = steal and escape. Example: They made off with the jewels.

notes.made over: Make over = give ownership, or redecorate.

q: We're ___ a big storm tonight, so bring the plants in.
explain: Be in for = going to experience (often bad). Example: You're in for a surprise!

notes.out for: Be out for = trying to get.
notes.up for: Be up for = willing to do.
notes.on for: On for isn't used this way.

q: Is anyone ___ a game of chess?
explain: Be up for = keen to do. Example: Who's up for pizza?

notes.down for: Down for = on a list for.

q: The sloth's fur is ___ with tiny green algae.
explain: Teem with = be full of living things. Example: The river teems with fish.

notes.swarming to: Swarming to isn't the pattern: swarm with.
notes.bursting out: Bursting out doesn't take with here.
notes.filling up: Filling up with is possible but doesn't mean full of living things.

q: The excitement ___ off after the first week of the holidays.
explain: Wear off = gradually disappear. Example: The anaesthetic wore off.

notes.wore out: Wear out = become tired, or damaged by use.
notes.took: Take off = remove, or succeed quickly.

q: Please don't ___ the issue. Tell me what happened.
explain: Skirt around (an issue) = avoid talking about it. Example: She skirted around the question.

notes.rush around: Rush around = hurry from place to place.

q: The new games console ___ instantly with teenagers.
explain: Catch on = become popular. Example: The trend caught on fast.

notes.caught up: Catch up = reach the same level.
notes.caught out: Catch out = trick someone into a mistake.

q: The tricky question was designed to ___ careless readers.
explain: Catch someone out = trick them into a mistake. Example: The quiz caught me out.

notes.catch up: Catch up = reach the same level.

q: Winning the science fair was the icing on the ___ after a great year.
explain: The icing on the cake = something that makes a good situation even better. Example: The sunny weather was the icing on the cake.

notes.biscuit: Biscuit isn't used in this idiom.
notes.bun: Bun isn't used in this idiom.
notes.pie: Pie isn't used in this idiom.

q: Finding the lost puppy was like looking for a needle in a ___.
explain: A needle in a haystack = almost impossible to find. Example: Finding one shell on the beach was a needle in a haystack.

notes.field: Field isn't used in this idiom.
notes.forest: Forest isn't used in this idiom.
notes.barn: Barn isn't used in this idiom.

q: Let's not count our ___ before they hatch; the final isn't over.
explain: Don't count your chickens before they hatch = don't be too sure of success. Example: We might win, but let's not count our chickens.

notes.eggs: Eggs are what hatch, but the idiom counts chickens.
notes.ducks: Ducks isn't used in this idiom.
notes.birds: Birds isn't used in this idiom.

q: The new robotics club is still finding its ___.
explain: Find your feet = become confident in a new situation. Example: It took me a week to find my feet.

notes.legs: Legs is used in 'have legs' (last a long time).
notes.hands: Hands isn't used in this idiom.

q: We're on the same ___ about the project, so let's start.
explain: On the same page = in agreement. Example: Are we all on the same page?

q: The plan to sneak a puppy into school was doomed from the ___.
explain: From the outset = from the beginning. Example: It was clear from the outset.

q: Missing the bus turned out to be a blessing in ___: we saw a rainbow.
explain: A blessing in disguise = something bad that turns out good. Example: Losing that game was a blessing in disguise.

notes.secret: Secret isn't used in this idiom.
notes.hiding: Hiding isn't used in this idiom.
notes.costume: Costume isn't used in this idiom.

q: The final exam is just around the ___.
explain: Just around the corner = coming very soon. Example: Summer is just around the corner.

notes.bend: Bend isn't used in this idiom.
notes.street: Street isn't used in this idiom.
notes.block: Block isn't used in this idiom.

q: He's always first to volunteer: he's as keen as ___.
explain: As keen as mustard = very enthusiastic (British). Example: The new players are keen as mustard.

notes.honey: Honey is for sweet, not keen.
notes.pepper: Pepper isn't used in this simile.
notes.lemon: Lemon isn't used in this simile.

q: She was over the ___ when she got the lead role.
explain: Over the moon = extremely happy. Example: I was over the moon with my results.

notes.stars: Stars isn't used in this idiom.
notes.sun: Sun isn't used in this idiom.
notes.clouds: Clouds is in 'on cloud nine', a different idiom.

q: Building the treehouse cost an arm and a ___.
explain: Cost an arm and a leg = be very expensive. Example: The tickets cost an arm and a leg.

notes.foot: Foot isn't used in this idiom.
notes.hand: Hand isn't used in this idiom.
notes.head: Head isn't used in this idiom.

q: I'll ___ on it and give you my answer tomorrow.
explain: Sleep on it = wait until tomorrow before deciding. Example: Don't decide now; sleep on it.

q: The ___ of the comet's path took months of calculation.
explain: Predict → prediction (the act of predicting). Example: weather predictions.

notes.predictability: Predictability = how easy something is to predict.

q: The wizard found himself in quite a ___: no wand, no map, no friends.
explain: Predicament = a difficult situation. Example: How did we get into this predicament?

notes.precaution: Precaution = an action to prevent harm.

q: Wear goggles as a ___ when you do the experiment.
explain: A precaution = something done to avoid danger. Example: as a precaution.

notes.prevention: Prevention = stopping something, not a single action you take 'as a'.

q: The surgeon robot works with incredible ___.
explain: Precise → precision (noun). Example: She drew the map with precision.

notes.precaution: Precaution = an action to avoid danger.
notes.preciseness of: Preciseness of needs a noun after it.

q: Her ___ to detail made her the best map-maker in the kingdom.
explain: Attention to detail = care with small things. Example: great attention to detail.

q: The ___ of the dodo was caused by humans.
explain: Extinct → extinction (noun). Example: the extinction of the dinosaurs.

notes.extinguisher: Extinguisher = a device that puts out fires.

q: The robot's behaviour was completely ___: nobody knew what it would do.
explain: un- + predictable = can't be predicted. Example: unpredictable weather.

notes.unpredicted: Unpredicted = not expected, for a specific event.

q: The ___ between the two theories is tiny.
explain: Discrepancy = a difference that shouldn't be there. Example: a discrepancy in the figures.

notes.discretion: Discretion = good judgement, or keeping secrets.

q: Please use your ___ when sharing the surprise party plans.
explain: Discretion = carefulness about what you say. Example: I trust your discretion.

q: Owls are ___ creatures, hunting mostly at night.
explain: Nocturnal = active at night. Example: Bats are nocturnal.

notes.nomadic: Nomadic = moving from place to place.

q: Some desert tribes and reindeer herders lead a ___ life, always on the move.
explain: Nomadic = moving from place to place. Example: a nomadic people.

notes.sedentary: Sedentary = sitting a lot, or staying in one place.
